sections.heading: Before you travel to Guinea-Bissau
sections.text:
Check the UK government’s [travel advice for Guinea-Bissau](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/guinea-bissau) before you book, and again shortly before you go. It covers safety, local laws, health risks and the latest entry rules.

- Passport: most countries expect it to be valid for at least six months after you arrive, with blank pages for stamps. If yours is close to expiry, renew it first.
- Health: check the NHS fitfortravel website for Guinea-Bissau at least eight weeks before you travel, in case you need vaccinations or malaria tablets. Some countries ask for a yellow fever certificate if you’ve recently been somewhere with yellow fever.
- Insurance: take out travel insurance that covers medical treatment and getting you home, and check it’s valid for Guinea-Bissau.
- Bookings: carry copies of your return ticket and accommodation, as border officers can ask to see them.

We go through the entry requirements for your passport when we prepare your application, so you know exactly what to carry.

faqs.q: Do British citizens need a visa for Guinea-Bissau?
faqs.a: Yes, a visa is needed and should be arranged before you travel. We confirm the current process for your trip.

faqs.q: How long does a Guinea-Bissau visa take?
faqs.a: Usually a few working days, but processing times vary. Apply at least a week before you travel, and earlier in busy seasons.

faqs.q: Can you apply for my Guinea-Bissau visa for me?
faqs.a: Yes. Use our online form: upload your passport and we fill in your details, then we complete and check the Guinea-Bissau visa application and submit it for you.

faqs.q: Do I need travel insurance for Guinea-Bissau?
faqs.a: We strongly recommend it. Choose a policy that covers medical treatment and repatriation, and check it’s valid for your destination before you go.
